newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland sells its Kemijoki A stock for FIM 2.1 bln.
newsitem.headline: Finland sells its Kemijoki A stock for FIM 2.1 bln.

text.p: The government said on Tuesday it had agreed to sell the state's 26,764 A shares in power producer Kemijoki Oy to the company's other owners Enso Oy, UPM-Kymmene and Imatran Voima (IVO).
"The transaction price is 2.1 billion markka," the ministry of trade and industry said in a statement.
The state would keep its B shares which give it a two-thirds majority of votes, it said. The A shares would be transferred to the buyers on April 1.

The state also offered Finland's northern electricity utilities the option to buy 6,565 A shares at the terms agreed with Enso, UPM and IVO, which would mean a total price of about 500 million markka, the ministry said.

"If the northern utilities use their option, Imatran Voima will own 62 percent of A shares, UPM-Kymmene Oy 19 percent, the city of Helsinki about four percent and Enso over two percent. Northern Finland's utilities' stake would rise to about 13 percent," the ministry said.
